comment: Port map for netlists/ctle_sp.cir. The tool turns this into port
sources on the named nets, for both the .sp sweep and the .ac
characterisation the model is fitted from, so the two see the
z0 in = 50 ohm: the receiver input is terminated to 100 ohm
differential by RT1/RT2 in the deck, which 2 x 50 ohm ports match.
z0 out = RD = 1000 ohm: the output IS a 1 kohm load node. A 50 ohm
port there would load the node to 47.6 ohm and measure a circuit
nobody builds, 26.4 dB down on this one.
Differential references are 2*z0: 100 ohm in, 2000 ohm out.
bias natural: each port's DC is the net's own operating-point
voltage, so no DC current flows through its z0 and the sweep
linearises about the operating point work/ctle.cir has. Measured
on a source follower, a port written DC 0 instead moved the node
from 243.8 mV to 7.7 mV and S21 by 7.8 dB.
